messages:
oliver (oncall): SLO alert just fired for p99 gateway timeouts in euw1, multiple customer tickets about 502/timeout spikes. alertbot posted details. cc @maya @jonah
alertbot: [ALERT] euw1.gateway.p99_latency > 1200ms for 6m, affected_teams=multiple, ticket_ids=[#6421,#6423] :rotating_light:
support-ops: Customers reporting sudden 5xx for text.generate endpoint, started ~10:12 UTC. One customer reports consistent repro with a 3-token prompt hitting a 504 after ~1.2s of server processing. Ticket 6421 has logs attached.
maya (sre): Looking at dashboard -> https://console.redwood.ai/d/euw1/gateway-latency?from=now-15m  there is a p99 jump and simultaneous surge of 5xx fraction on /v1/text.generate. Notable: spike correlates with host pool "inference-euw1-22" CPU steal and kube restarts.
jonah (platform): I see CI rollout completed at 10:05 UTC for the routing proxy. Rolling back that deploy would be low-risk. Can we confirm link between deploy and 5xx?
oliver (oncall): support-ops attached request_id list: [req_7a2, req_7a3, req_7b0]. Logs show upstream timeout to model-worker with: "RPC error: upstream read timeout" repeated.
maya (sre): Quick checks:
- logs query: service:gateway status:[500..599] AND path:"/v1/text.generate" | count() by upstream, pod
- traces: sample rate for gateway->worker path is 1% currently, likely missing coverage for correlated spans.
- check node metrics: vmstat/iowait on nodes in pool inference-euw1-22
jonah (platform): Running logs query now, output shows 70% of 5xx coming from pod inference-proxy-22 and errors show "context deadline exceeded" from grpc dial to worker pool.
maya (sre): probable root cause: rollout bumped proxy concurrency/keepalive defaults causing connection saturation to workers; worker side started rejecting or timing out under burst.
support-ops: Customers want repro steps so they can confirm. Any temporary mitigations?
maya (sre): Immediate mitigations:
- rollback proxy rollout (low-risk)
- increase gateway->worker dial timeout to 3s in runtime config: `gateway.worker.dial_timeout=3s`
- enable fallback route to smaller model variant for the affected customers via routing policy (route: model=v0.9 -> v0.7)
jonah (platform): I'll stage a rollback to previous proxy image and patch dial timeout. Pushing canary to 1 node first. ETA 8m.
oliver (oncall): Noted. Also add temporary sampling bump for traces to 25% for gateway->worker to capture correlated spans: `tracing.sampling.gateway_worker=0.25`.
alertbot: Incident timeline: triggered 10:13 UTC, p99 peaked 10:14-10:18 UTC.
support-ops: Passing rollback plan and temporary mitigations to customers. They're asking if this is billing-related (token billing hiccup). Any signs?
maya (sre): No evidence of billing system involvement in traces or logs. Auth tokens look valid; authz service responses normal. 5xx from proxy->worker layer.
jonah (platform): Canary rollback succeeded on node inference-proxy-21, initial metrics show p99 dropping from 1400ms -> 220ms for that node within 30s. Proceeding with full rollback.
oliver (oncall): After rollback p99 trending down cluster-wide. Closing customer ticket drafts with repro steps and mitigations. Followups:
- postmortem template: include deploy diff + kernel/pod oom/restart counts + trace sampling gap notes
- add alert: correlate alerting query to upstream error ratio per pod to avoid noisy pool-wide SLO fires
- add playback test: synthetic traffic at small concurrency hitting /v1/text.generate under new proxy config before rollout
maya (sre): I'll open the postmortem and assign action items. Also recommend increasing pre-rollout trace sampling to 5% for 30m after deploys that touch routing.
support-ops: Thanks all, updating customers. :thumbsup:
